note: Written by hand for test_phone_scam_detect.js. Scam texts follow the wording of the tech support scam pop-ups reported by Microsoft, the FTC and Malwarebytes, with fiction numbers (555-01xx). Normal texts are typical contact, restaurant, bank, news and support pages. layout is a string of letters for what the page looks like: o = pop-up holding the number, f = full screen, b = bare page (almost no links, no menu or footer), a = big red or orange areas.

normal.name: news scam article 1
normal.text: Police warn of tech support scam. Officers say scammers pose as Microsoft support, telling victims that their computer is infected with a virus and that they should call 1-800-555-0100 immediately. One Calgary woman lost $3,000 after allowing the caller remote access. Do not call the number on a pop-up, police say.

normal.name: news scam article 2
normal.text: How the fake virus pop-up works. A page fills the screen with a loud warning: your computer is locked, do not close this window, call Windows Support now. Researchers found the number leads to a call centre that charges hundreds of dollars for useless software. The FTC says to close the browser and ignore the page.

normal.name: news scam article 3
normal.text: Seniors targeted by Apple support impostors. The Better Business Bureau reports a rise in pop-ups claiming a Mac has been hacked and urging people to call a toll-free number. If you see one, restart the browser. Real companies do not put phone numbers in warnings.

normal.name: news scam article 4
normal.text: Geek Squad invoice scam hits inboxes. Messages claim you were charged $389.99 for a protection plan and tell you to call a number to dispute it. Security firm Malwarebytes says the number connects to scammers who ask to install AnyDesk. Never call numbers in unexpected invoices.

normal.name: news scam article 5
normal.text: Consumer protection tips. Scammers call and say there is suspicious activity on your account. They ask you to read out a code. Hang up and call the real number on your card. Report fraud to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at 1-888-495-8501.

normal.name: news scam article 6
normal.text: Browser lockers explained. These pages go full screen, play an alarm and show a fake Microsoft warning with a phone number. Press Escape or close the tab. Your computer is not infected. Do not call the number shown.

normal.name: microsoft scam help
normal.text: Protect yourself from tech support scams. Microsoft will never send unsolicited pop-ups asking you to call a number. If you see a message saying your computer is infected, close the window. To report a scam call 1-800-555-0199 or use the report form.

normal.name: long article with number
normal.text: Chapter 12. The story so far. She picked up the phone, hesitated, and dialled 555-0142 from memory. The line rang for a long time. Behind her the radio warned of a storm and she knew she had to leave the house before it hit. Do not turn back, she told herself. Outside the street was empty.
